name: EvilTokens
description: EvilTokens is a turnkey Phishing-as-a-Service (PhaaS) kit that surfaced in cybercrime communities in mid-February 2026 and was publicly detailed by Sekoia in March 2026. Sold via Telegram bots run by 'eviltokensadmin', it automates Microsoft OAuth device-code phishing against Microsoft 365 and Entra ID tenants, harvesting Primary Refresh Tokens that grant access to Outlook, Exchange Online, SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams and Azure. Post-compromise, the kit's AI-augmented automation performs reconnaissance, mailbox rule manipulation, and email harvesting to fuel Business Email Compromise fraud at scale. Microsoft and partners observed 10-15 distinct campaigns per day since mid-March 2026, with infrastructure spanning over 1,000 phishing domains and victims confirmed across the Americas, Europe, the Middle East, Asia and Oceania.

ttps.notes: Abuses OAuth 2.0 device authorization flow to capture Primary Refresh Tokens and downstream access tokens
Lures direct victims to enter attacker-supplied device codes at microsoft.com/devicelogin
Stolen tokens used to authenticate directly to Microsoft Graph, Exchange Online, and Azure without credentials
Built-in webmail interface and automation harvest mailbox content from Exchange Online via Graph API
Token exchange to mint additional scoped tokens for SharePoint, OneDrive, Substrate and Teams
Operator-managed pool of 1,000+ lookalike phishing domains rotated across campaigns
AI-generated lure content impersonates IT, HR, and partner organizations to drive device-code entry

notable_techniques: Fully automated Telegram-bot storefront ('eviltokensadmin') for kit purchase, configuration, and victim management
AI-powered post-compromise automation: auto-generates reconnaissance summaries and BEC lure emails from harvested mailbox content
Token exchange chain converts a single device-code grant into Outlook, Graph, Azure, Substrate, and SharePoint access
Built-in webmail viewer lets low-skill affiliates browse and exfiltrate victim mailboxes without separate tooling
10-15 new distinct campaigns per day observed since mid-March 2026, run from a 1,000+ domain rotating infrastructure
Rapid feature iteration — kit updated continuously by the operator in response to detection coverage
detection_opportunities: Sign-ins via the OAuth device authorization flow ('urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code') from unfamiliar apps or locations
Microsoft Entra ID sign-in logs showing device code grants followed immediately by Graph API calls to Mail, Files, and SharePoint
New inbox rules or mailbox forwarding created shortly after an unfamiliar device-code authentication
User-reported prompts to visit microsoft.com/devicelogin and enter a code received via chat, email, or QR code
Conditional Access policies blocking or flagging legacy/device-code auth flows for non-shared-device scenarios
Anomalous Graph API enumeration of Teams, OneDrive, and SharePoint shortly after a new token issuance
Outbound traffic to newly registered lookalike domains hosting EvilTokens phishing pages
response_playbook: Review Entra ID sign-in logs for OAuth device-code grant flows from unfamiliar apps or locations.
Audit for new inbox rules or mailbox-forwarding rules created shortly after a device-code authentication event.
Brief users that legitimate services rarely require visiting microsoft.com/devicelogin with a code received via chat, email, or QR code.
Restrict the OAuth device-code auth flow via Conditional Access for non-shared-device scenarios.
Hunt for anomalous Graph API enumeration of Teams/OneDrive/SharePoint following new token issuance.
Block known EvilTokens phishing infrastructure (rotating lookalike domains) at the email/web gateway.
